validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE is not independently confirmed. The row's ONLY cited support (wiki_citations) is 'OPEC Annual Statistics Bulletin 2012, p.75' — a country-level oil/gas statistics table that does NOT name any pipeline. I fetched that PDF through url_verifier: it returns 200 but does NOT contain the tokens 'Aindar' or 'Shedgum' (FAIL), so it cannot support this line. Every other web hit for 'Aindar-Shedgum gas pipeline' (WebSearch, multiple queries incl. Arabic-adjacent trade terms) traces back to the gem.wiki page itself or restates its numbers — no independent origin. GulfPub PE World Map's Saudi gas roster (20 features, SA is its best-covered country) has NO Ain Dar–Shedgum entry (it lists Qatif-Berri, Abqaiq-Qatif, East-West, MGS/MGS2/MGS3, Fadhili, Jafurah) — so the independent dataset does not corroborate this pipe. What IS real and well-sourced is the GEOGRAPHY: Ain Dar ('Ayn Dar) and Shedgum are the two northernmost adjacent production areas of the Ghawar field, ~13–19 km apart at the GOSP level (Wikipedia Ghawar Field; DMS/dmsuniverse project listings), and a short associated-gas line between Ain Dar and the Shedgum gas plant is physically plausible. But plausibility is not confirmation: no independent source states a 34 km / 12-inch Aindar–Shedgum GAS pipeline exists. This is a GEM-only entity resting on a non-naming citation. Also note P1924 shares the 2022-07-19 update stamp with a whole block of P19xx Ghawar lines (P1905/1907/1908/1913/1917–1920 etc.), suggesting a single bulk import whose provenance was never re-verified.

validity.recommendation: If retained, reassess whether a 12-inch / 34 km line carrying 'Aindar' field gas into the Shedgum gas plant is in-scope as a transmission pipeline or is field-to-plant gathering/feeder. Decide alongside the many other small intra-Ghawar P19xx lines.
validity.researcher_notes: Even if it exists, the profile reads as a GATHERING/FEEDER line, not a gas-transmission trunk: FuelSource='Aindar' (a producing field, i.e. this carries Ain Dar associated/field gas), small 12-inch bore, 34 km, endpoint = Shedgum gas PLANT. That is the signature of field-GOSP-to-processing-plant gathering rather than a sales-gas transmission trunk (contrast the 46–56 inch MGS/East-West trunks). Secondary to the existence concern; flagging so a scope decision is made for the intra-Ghawar P19xx cluster rather than silently passing.

Corridor is only LOOSELY bounded: I could not source the actual routing or the exact Ain Dar GOSP location. Endpoint coordinates are APPROXIMATE and defensible from named Ghawar geography, NOT sourced-precise — Shedgum ~25.68N/49.40E is a commonly reported location for the Shedgum plant; Ain Dar ~26.0N/49.2E is the approximate center of the Ain Dar area. Straight-line between these is ~35–40 km, roughly consistent with the sheet's 34 km, which is the only quantitative cross-check available and does not by itself prove the pipe. No waypoints sourced.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established only at the AREA level from Ghawar geography (Ain Dar and Shedgum are adjacent northern Ghawar production areas per Wikipedia Ghawar Field, verifier OK with tokens 'Ain Dar','Shedgum','Ghawar').
